clue.text: Dog, one with puppies far from relaxed

parts.note: a mother, MA, is one with young; a bitch with puppies is a mother
stiff means tense, the opposite of relaxed

explanation.surface: A dog owner describes a nervous mother dog fretting over her new litter.
explanation.walkthrough: MA, a mother, is the one with puppies; STIFF is tense, far from relaxed.
explanation.definitionFit: A mastiff is a large, powerful breed of guard dog, so it is an example of a dog.

clue.text: Sensation I hate, skin in morning tickled?

indicators.note: tickled suggests being stirred up, so these letters are jumbled
the skin of a word is its outer layer, its first and last letters

parts.note: the word whose outside letters are taken

explanation.surface: Someone hates the feeling of being tickled first thing in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skin in' takes M and G, the outer letters of 'morning', which join I HATE before 'tickled' mixes them all.
explanation.definitionFit: A megahit is a huge success, a smash or sensation.

clue.text: One day, wise guy!

parts.note: a solo is a performance by one
Mon is the abbreviation for Monday

explanation.surface: An exclamation at a smart alec on some day.
explanation.walkthrough: Wise guy usually means a smart alec; here it is meant literally.
explanation.definitionFit: King Solomon of the Bible is proverbial for his wisdom.

clue.text: Best possible declaration of player holding all the cards?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: perfect, the best one could hope for

definitions.text: declaration of player holding all the cards?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: read as ..., the announcement of the card player who has the pack to hand out

explanation.walkthrough: Holding all the cards usually means having every advantage; here it is literally the dealer with the pack.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means perfect; split in two it is the dealer's statement at the card table.

clue.text: My time in Royal Ascot attire?

indicators.note: in places time inside the hat phrase

parts.note: Royal Ascot, an English racing event, is famous for elaborate fancy hats

explanation.surface: Asking whether some outfit for a famous horse race will do.
explanation.walkthrough: Royal Ascot is an English summer race meeting where spectators wear extravagant hats. 'My' is an exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of mild surprise; well I never would be another.

clue.text: Man on journey singing for his supper?

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it

parts.note: a bus is the vehicle of a journey, standing in for the trip itself
a king is one of the men in chess

explanation.surface: A man travelling somewhere sings to earn a meal along the way.
explanation.walkthrough: Man suggests a person, but it is a chess piece; the question mark flags that busking is only loosely singing for one's supper.
explanation.definitionFit: Busking is performing music in the street for money, the modern way of earning a meal by performance.

clue.text: Country lacks it, mind

indicators.note: lacks means is without, so these letters are dropped from the country

parts.note: Britain is a country

explanation.surface: A nation is short of good sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The brain is the organ of thought, used loosely for intellect.

clue.text: Tom, perhaps, cracks up over American film

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the first part above the second
in a down clue, up means the letters are read bottom to top

parts.note: a tom is a male cat, an example of one
raps are sharp blows or cracks

explanation.surface: A tomcat falls about laughing over an American movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracks up' looks like laughing, but cracks is RAPS and up reverses CAT RAPS to SPARTAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Spartacus is the 1960 Kubrick epic starring Kirk Douglas as the rebel gladiator.

clue.text: Isn't trained soldier, say, prepared in advance?

indicators.note: trained means trimmed or directed into a new shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of isn't, apostrophe ignored
a soldier ant is one kind of ant, so ant is an example

explanation.surface: Questioning whether a soldier is drilled or ready.
explanation.definitionFit: Instant food or coffee is made beforehand so it needs only water at the point of use.

clue.text: Share costs with encouraging words from husband?

parts.note: go is a shout of encouragement
my old Dutch is Cockney slang a husband uses for his wife, from duchess

explanation.surface: Splitting the bill, with a spouse urging it on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go, Dutch!' reads as a husband cheering on his wife; Dutch is Cockney for wife.
explanation.definitionFit: To go Dutch is the idiom for each person paying their own share of a bill.

clue.text: Device ultimately dividing measure of liquid in vessel

indicators.note: dividing means splitting the measure of liquid by sitting within it

parts.note: a gallon is a unit of liquid volume

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the last letter of device is used

parts.note: the word whose final letter is taken

explanation.surface: A gadget splits a quantity of liquid inside some container.
explanation.walkthrough: The E at the end of 'Device' splits GALLON after its L's.
explanation.definitionFit: A galleon is a large sailing ship of the past, a type of vessel at sea.

clue.text: Under protection of goddess, a maiden from the East raised

indicators.note: an across clue read from the East runs right to left, so the letters go backwards
being under the protection of these words means the letters lie sheltered inside them

parts.note: the letters sit across the end of goddess, the a and the start of maiden

explanation.surface: A girl from the Orient grows up sheltered by a deity.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside 'goddESS A MAiden' sit DESSAMA; 'from the East' reads them right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: Amassed means gathered together or collected, as money is raised for a cause.

clue.text: Chewing up hay, animal like the yak?

indicators.note: chewing up food mashes it into a new arrangement, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A beast munching hay is compared to a yak.
explanation.walkthrough: HAY and ANIMAL together have exactly the nine letters needed.
explanation.definitionFit: The yak is native to the high Himalayan region of Tibet and Nepal, so it is a mountain beast of that range.

clue.text: Brown bread, dead!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to brown under a grill, as a verb
third meaning: slang for doomed or finished

explanation.walkthrough: Brown bread is also rhyming slang for dead, which tempts you to read the clue as one phrase; it is three separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers grilling bread to brown it, the grilled slice itself, and slang for someone who is doomed.

clue.text: Triad shot in the arm

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the ... triad, the chord built on the keynote of a scale
second meaning: a boost or pick-me-up

explanation.walkthrough: Triad suggests a Chinese crime gang, but it is the musical chord on the keynote.
explanation.definitionFit: In music the keynote chord is called by this name, and figuratively a reviving boost is one too.

clue.text: Buddy and girl nearly finished drink

parts.note: champ is an informal form of address like buddy or mate

indicators.note: nearly finished means the end is left off, so the last letter goes

parts.note: Agnes is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A pal and a girl have almost polished off their drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Champagne is the sparkling wine from the French region of that name.

clue.text: Game for children providing silence on journey

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it

parts.note: a hop is a short trip, especially a short flight
to scotch a rumour is to silence it or put an end to it

explanation.surface: Something to keep kids quiet on a long trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopscotch is a playground game where children hop through numbered squares chalked on the ground.

clue.text: Cold will be gone soon

definitions.meaning: second meaning: dying, about to perish

explanation.definitionFit: The word describes freezing weather, and literally describes something dying or about to expire.

clue.text: Degree secured by US lexicographer, developer of online site

indicators.note: secured by means held fast inside, so the degree sits within the lexicographer's name

parts.note: Noah Webster compiled the classic American dictionary
MA, Master of Arts, is a university degree

explanation.surface: A dictionary writer earns a qualification and goes on to build a website.
explanation.definitionFit: A webmaster is the person who builds and maintains a website.

clue.text: So-and-so, with task almost entirely messed up

indicators.note: messed up means jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: almost entirely means all but the end, so the final letter goes

explanation.surface: A person bungles a job almost completely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost entirely' trims TASK to TAS, and 'messed up' scrambles WITH and TAS together.
explanation.definitionFit: A whatsit is a stand-in word for a thing or person whose name escapes you, like thingummy.

clue.text: Charlie's gift-wrapped instrument

indicators.note: wrapped means enclosed, so the gift goes round the fool

parts.note: a boon is a blessing or gift
a charlie is a fool, an ass; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: Someone has been given a musical instrument as a present.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlie is British slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: The bassoon is a large woodwind instrument with a low register.

clue.text: Money from Cape Town, say, for fabric

indicators.note: from places the money after the country it comes from

parts.note: SA, South Africa, is the country containing Cape Town, an example of it
tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: Cash earned in South Africa is spent on cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Satin is a smooth, glossy woven cloth, often silk.

clue.text: Effective relation

definitions.meaning: first meaning: having a strong effect
second meaning: the act of recounting

explanation.definitionFit: A telling argument is a striking one, and a relation is a narration or account of events.

clue.text: Cross being clear, shown

parts.note: nett means clear of deductions, as clear profit
led means guided, as one is shown the way

explanation.surface: Someone is angry at being cleared yet still exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: Nettled means irritated or annoyed, as stung by a nettle.

clue.text: Teller of tales in a show that's retrospective

indicators.note: retrospective means looking back, so the word for show is read backwards

parts.note: to pose is to display or put on a show

explanation.surface: A storyteller appears in a show looking back over his career.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop is the ancient Greek storyteller credited with the famous animal fables.

clue.text: Early high-flier, one occupying river bed

parts.note: the Test is a river in Hampshire, England

indicators.note: occupying means sitting inside, so one goes into the bed

parts.note: a plot is a bed of ground for planting
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A pioneer of flight lies in a riverbed.
explanation.walkthrough: The Test is a chalk-stream river in Hampshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A test pilot flies new aircraft before anyone else, so is an early flier of each plane.

clue.text: Sticky delay

definitions.meaning: first meaning: covered in tar, gummy
second meaning: to linger or wait

explanation.definitionFit: Pronounced one way it means tacky like tar; another way it means to linger.

clue.text: Leaders in public roles, invariably obnoxious, rather superior among brothers

indicators.note: leaders are the front letters, so each word's first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A monastic head is said to be consistently unpleasant in public.
explanation.definitionFit: A prior is the head of a priory, ranking just below an abbot in a monastic order.

clue.text: Freeloader beginning to scrounge, stinker?

indicators.note: beginning to means the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: the word whose first letter is taken
a ponger is something that pongs, or smells bad

explanation.surface: A cadger starts to beg and is called a smelly wretch.
explanation.walkthrough: To pong is British slang for to smell bad.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponger lives off the generosity of others, which is just what a freeloader does.

clue.text: First sign

definitions.meaning: first meaning: occurring at the beginning, as an adjective
second meaning: to mark with one's ..., as a verb

explanation.definitionFit: The word means at the beginning, and also to endorse a document with the opening letters of your name.

clue.text: Endeavour to nurse queen where skin undergoing treatment

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close in the arms, so the queen goes inside

parts.note: to try is to endeavour
Anne was a queen of England

explanation.surface: A queen is cared for at a clinic where skin conditions are treated.
explanation.walkthrough: Skin here is animal hide, not a patient's.
explanation.definitionFit: A tannery is the works where animal hides are cured into leather.

clue.text: Containing anger, son of Jacob shut up

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the son holds the anger

parts.note: Gad was one of Jacob's twelve sons in Genesis
rage is fury, anger

explanation.surface: One of Jacob's sons holds in his fury and stops talking.
explanation.definitionFit: Garaged means put away and locked in a garage, as a car is shut up for the night.
